finding.claim: The unscoped /invoice/<inv_id> route returns the full invoice record for any existing ID with no authentication and no ownership check, enabling broken object-level authorization (IDOR).
finding.source: inv_id path parameter (invoices.py:7-8); no auth required by the route.
finding.sink: jsonify(inv) returning the complete invoice, including the customer field (invoices.py:10).

trace.note: Route /invoice/<inv_id> registered with no auth decorator.
Full invoice record returned to the caller.

finding.guards_checked: No ownership comparison against g.user (contrast /my/invoice/ at invoices.py:16); no login or role check in this file; no before_request hook or auth decorator defined in this file. Exploitation requires the route to be served in production and invoice IDs to be enumerable or guessable; if IDs are unguessable UUIDs, impact is limited to IDs leaked elsewhere.

verdict.guard_found: none. The only ownership check is at invoices.py:16-17 and applies only to /my/invoice/<inv_id> (invoices.py:13-18). A grep of the directory found no before_request, before_app_request, login_required, g.user assignment, after_request, or blueprint hook covering the unscoped route.
verdict.reason: The route at invoices.py:7-10 has no authentication or ownership check, so an anonymous caller who knows or can guess an invoice ID gets the full record from jsonify(inv) at invoices.py:10; the trace matches the code. Impact depends on whether IDs are enumerable, as the candidate notes, but that limits severity and does not refute the missing access control.
